## What you build today

A brushless motor with a custom shaft pressed into its rotor bell, paired to
the Faulhaber gearbox, with the sun gear and the sensor magnet installed.

## Before you arrive

| | |
|---|---|
| **Parts** | AS2303 KV1500 motor, 4 mm steel rod, Faulhaber 23.04:1 gearbox, M2.5×10 screws |
| **Tools** | Circlip pliers, manual arbor press, lathe (booked), cutting oil |
| **Read** | This page, and the *Motor shaft* section below in full before touching the motor |

## How the transmission works

The motor is connected via a custom shaft to a gearbox with a **23.04:1**
reduction by Faulhaber.[^1] Both parts are held in place by 3D-printed plates.
The output shaft of the gearbox has its own bearing on the inside of the
gearbox, and is also supported mid-way on the shaft by a 4×8 mm flanged
bearing. This leaves **5 mm of shaft length free** for the crank to be mounted
on. A flat on the shaft helps lock the rotation of the M3 screw extending
through the crank.

[^1]: [Faulhaber gearhead reduction ratios](https://www.faulhaber.com/fileadmin/Import/Media/DE_GEARHEADS_REDUCTION_RATIOS.pdf) (accessed 20.02.2024).

## Which motor do you have? {#sec-motor-variant}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Black --- AS2303 KV1500 (new)

![](/Fig/TMO-AS2303-1500.jpg){width=45%}

The propeller horn **cannot** be separated from the bell. You will remove the
two screws, then clamp the bell in a lathe using the stock shaft and machine
it down (step 4 below).

### Blue --- AT2303 KV1500 (old)

![](/Fig/TMO-AT2303-1500.jpg){width=45%}

The horn is a separate part and comes off easily. Skip the lathe operation.

:::

## Motor shaft

To pair the motor with the gearbox, the shaft of the brushless motor needs to
be replaced. This is a delicate operation --- the motor's structure is mostly
aluminium and quite thin, for weight savings.

1. Remove the circlip on the shaft with the special pliers. **Don't lose it,
   nor the brass ring.**

2. Separate the rotor from the stator delicately, by hand.

3. Press the shaft out of the rotor bell.

   ::: {.callout-warning}
   ## Never load the bell radially

   Press the shaft out very carefully, making sure to never apply forces
   radially on the bell. Use the manual press with appropriate support below
   the bell to avoid deforming the dome shape. **Do not squeeze the bell with a
   vice, or even by hand.**
   :::

4. Remove the propeller horn, which is not needed --- see
   [the tabs above](#sec-motor-variant) for which case applies to you. On the
   black motor, machine the bell as follows:

   ::: {layout-ncol=3}
   ![Stock bell](/Fig/bell_machined1.jpg)

   ![Bring diameter down to 6 mm](/Fig/bell_machined2.jpg)

   ![Bring the length down to 2.5 mm](/Fig/bell_machined3.jpg)
   :::

5. Manufacture the new shaft from 4 mm diameter steel rod. It should have a
   **clearance fit** through the bearings and a **tight fit** on the rotor
   bell. See @fig-motor-shaft for exact dimensions.

   ::: {.callout-warning}
   ## Check your wall thickness before cutting

   21.5 mm is the shaft length **if the motor and the gearbox are separated by
   a 5.5 mm-thick wall**. If your wall is 4 mm thick, reduce the 8.5 mm segment
   to 7 mm, bringing the total length from 21.5 mm to 20 mm.
   :::

6. Press the new shaft into the bell, making sure not to press on the
   dome-shaped part of the bell without appropriate support underneath.

![Motor shaft dimensions](/Fig/shaft_drawing.png){#fig-motor-shaft width=70%}

## Gearbox assembly

The blue part of the gearbox is fixed on one side using the custom screws that
come with the gearbox, and with **M2.5×10** screws on the other.

::: {.callout-important}
## To be completed by the instructor

Sun gear installation and sensor magnet bonding are in the course project plan
but are not documented in the manufacturing guide. Add the magnet part number,
bonding agent, and the concentricity tolerance that matters for
[Module 4](04-control.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Checkpoint --- TA sign-off

Shaft seated, rotor spinning freely by hand with no wobble, gearbox mounted,
and the sensor magnet concentric with the shaft axis. An off-centre magnet
produces sensor faults that are very hard to diagnose two modules later.
:::
